steps.what: Choose appropriate baseline measures and administration conditions for monitoring the actual clinical question
inputs: existing patient history and authorized test protocols

steps.what: Administer the baseline measures and observe actual responses and administration limitations
outputs: actual baseline responses and observed conditions

steps.what: Check actual response entry and obtain baseline scores using the authorized scoring software
inputs: actual baseline responses and observed conditions
authorized test version and scoring rules

steps.what: Interpret whether the measures form a valid baseline for disease progression or recovery monitoring
inputs: actual baseline responses and observed conditions
outputs: clinician's baseline interpretation and comparability limitations

steps.what: Record and finish checking baseline scores, test versions, dates, conditions and interpretive limitations in the clinical record
inputs: clinician's baseline interpretation and comparability limitations

steps.what: Save the completed baseline record in the same clinical system

tasks.design: Keep authorized test administration and scoring in assessment software {OTHER}; configure a native baseline record template in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The neuropsychologist selects and interprets the measures, records actual scores and comparability limitations, finishes checking the record and saves it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated record headings add entry after establishing the actual baseline.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record fields can reuse existing patient and test identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: A baseline may not be comparable later if conditions or test versions change.
tasks.human_edge: Judge validity and preserve the conditions that qualify interpretation.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: neurobehavioral baselines require actual test responses, authorized scoring and clinical interpretation; record templates assist repeated metadata entry.

assumptions: OTHER is authorized neuropsychological assessment software; OPS_SYSTEM is the clinical record. Boundary includes the actual baseline and its recorded comparability conditions, not subsequent monitoring or a report send.

Clinician selects measures in s1 and produces actual responses and conditions in s2. Authorized scoring supplies scores from entered responses in s3; clinician supplies interpretation in s4. Missing responses or version identifiers require manual resolution, not inferred values.
Native record templates first. Shares are provisional; scoring is already software-assisted and its runtime earns no saving. Only repeated record metadata entry changes.
Gross 0.9 minus 0.2 upkeep gives 0.7 net. Same-system save is 1% fully retained. Checking is part of normal clinical record authoring, with no new self-approval step.
unknowns: Actual record metadata burden and baseline-template availability
research_questions: Can native baseline fields save entry without losing test-version and administration-condition details?

already_counted.description: Record and check actual baseline details

approvals.approved_version: complete checked baseline record at end of s5; edits void check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if fields already suffice; up to 0.4% with smaller metadata gains than central 0.7% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Educate and counsel individuals and families

steps.what: Consult relevant existing clinical context and approved educational material
outputs: source-checked context and relevant educational content

steps.what: Provide education or counseling to the individual and family, respond to concerns and check understanding
inputs: source-checked context and relevant educational content
outputs: education and counseling provided with clarified understanding

steps.what: Write and finish checking the ordinary clinical encounter note from the actual education or counseling provided
inputs: education and counseling provided with clarified understanding

steps.what: Save the completed encounter note in the same clinical record
outputs: saved education or counseling encounter note

tasks.design: Configure native approved-material references in {DOCS} and ordinary encounter-note fields in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The neuropsychologist provides the actual education or counseling and writes and checks the encounter note; no model substitutes for the therapeutic exchange.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source navigation and repeated note headings add small administrative effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native references and note templates can reduce those repeated actions.
tasks.still_hard: The individual's concern may differ from the question first expressed.
tasks.human_edge: Listen, clarify and respond in a way the family can understand.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: clinical counseling normally has an encounter record; native note fields and references assist metadata and navigation while counseling remains human.

assumptions: Model a clinical encounter that already includes ordinary clinical documentation. Verify that scope locally; do not create a new counseling note merely to obtain an administrative baseline. No separate report or family message is performed.

Clinical record owner supplies existing context; reference owner supplies approved material. Clinician produces actual encounter content in s2 and writes it in s3; no ambient recording or uncounted dictation is assumed.
Native templates first. Shares are unmeasured scenarios; reductions touch source navigation and repeated note headings only. All counseling and factual note content stays retained.
Gross 2.4 minus 0.3 upkeep gives 2.1 net. Same-system save is 1% fully retained; note checking stays in ordinary authoring without another approval step.
unknowns: Actual encounter-note requirement and metadata burden
research_questions: Does this clinical task actually include a separately timed encounter note, and do native fields reduce only repeated metadata?

already_counted.description: Verify references and complete the actual encounter note

incremental.description: Maintain approved references and encounter fields

approvals.approved_version: complete checked encounter note at end of s3; edits void check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if no separate clinical note or repeated navigation exists; up to 1% with smaller metadata gains than central 2.1% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Diagnose and treat pediatric learning conditions

steps.what: Review actual pediatric history, assessment evidence and developmental context
inputs: existing pediatric history and actual assessment evidence

steps.what: Diagnose pediatric conditions such as learning disabilities with developmental or organic bases using the actual evidence and uncertainty
Provide individualized treatment and adjust support to the child's actual response
inputs: child's actual response and family context
outputs: actual treatment provided and observed response

steps.what: Write and finish checking the clinical record of the actual formulation, treatment and response
inputs: actual treatment provided and observed response

steps.what: Save the completed pediatric entry in the same clinical record
outputs: saved actual pediatric diagnosis and treatment entry

tasks.design: Configure native evidence views and ordinary clinical entry fields in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The neuropsychologist makes the diagnostic formulation, provides treatment and records actual care; no generated diagnosis, treatment choice or educational eligibility decision is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Navigating evidence and repeating clinical entry identifiers add small overhead.
tasks.enabler_now: Native patient views and record templates can assist navigation and metadata entry.
tasks.still_hard: Developmental context and access barriers can change the meaning of a test finding.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the child and family rather than treating a score as a diagnosis.

ambition.what: No autonomous pediatric diagnosis or expanded caseload.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-8; pediatric clinical access and governance consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: clinical records can assist pediatric evidence retrieval and documentation, while diagnosis and treatment require clinician judgement.

assumptions: OPS_SYSTEM is the clinical record. Boundary includes evidence review, clinician diagnosis, actual treatment and existing clinical documentation. No referral send, prescription or eligibility determination is performed.

Existing clinicians supply actual history and assessment evidence with dates and source authors. Neuropsychologist supplies formulation and actual care content in s2-s3 and records it in s4; missing evidence stays unknown.
Native views and templates first. Shares are provisional; only navigation and repeated entry headings change. Verify actual clinical documentation scope and resolve shared encounter work at roll-up.
Gross 3.9 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 3.4 net. Same-system save is 1% fully retained. Finishing and checking the clinical entry is ordinary authoring, with no new approval task.
unknowns: Current evidence views and actual clinical-entry metadata effort
research_questions: Can native functions reduce navigation and headings without hiding clinical uncertainty or changing clinician decisions?

already_counted.description: Check source evidence and complete clinical documentation

incremental.description: Maintain evidence references and clinical entry fields

approvals.approved_version: complete checked pediatric entry at end of s4; edits void check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero when native views already suffice; up to 2% with smaller navigation and metadata gains than central 3.4% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep current through literature and professional exchange

steps.what: Find current neuropsychology literature through database searches and journal alerts
Read current literature and critically assess methods, findings and applicability to neuropsychology practice
outputs: clinician's critical understanding of current findings

steps.what: Talk with colleagues about current developments and their practical limits
inputs: clinician's critical understanding of current findings

steps.what: Participate in professional organizations or conferences to keep abreast of neuropsychology developments
inputs: actual professional events and organization activities

tasks.design: Configure native saved searches and journal alerts in the literature database {OTHER}. The neuropsychologist still reads the actual papers, discusses developments with colleagues and participates in professional events; generated summaries do not replace that work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated searches can make locating relevant current papers cumbersome.
tasks.enabler_now: Native search filters and saved searches can reuse the clinician's own topics.
tasks.still_hard: A relevant paper may have weak evidence or poor applicability.
tasks.human_edge: Critically assess methods and discuss implications with informed colleagues.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native journal searches and alerts can reduce repeated literature retrieval without replacing critical reading or professional exchange.

assumptions: OTHER is a bibliographic database and journal library. Boundary includes retrieval, actual reading, colleague discussion and professional participation; no separate review article, event booking or learning-record write is established.

Publishers supply actual bibliographic records with title, date and identifier; clinician supplies search topics. Missing full texts require manual access resolution rather than a generated substitute.
Native searches first. Shares are provisional and only retrieval changes. Gross 4 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 3.5 net; reading and participation stay fully retained.
unknowns: Current saved-search coverage and actual repeated-search effort
research_questions: Do saved searches reduce retrieval while retaining access to contrary or unexpected findings?

incremental.description: Review saved-search terms as topics change

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero when saved searches already suffice; up to 2% with smaller retrieval gains than central 3.5% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Neuropsychologists retain actual assessment, diagnosis, treatment, counseling and critical reading; native views and fields reduce small navigation and metadata tasks.
skills_to_grow: Check clinical source attribution and literature methods
role.ambitious_version: Traceable clinical records and current sources while clinical decisions remain with the neuropsychologist.
